target.title: fix(cron): throttle session reaper after persistence errors
target.body:
Closes #105188

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators with temporary session-store permission or disk errors would see the cron session reaper immediately retry on every timer tick, thrashing CPU and disk I/O instead of waiting for the normal cooldown.

## Why This Change Was Made

When `sweepCronRunSessions` hits a persistence failure, it already logs and returns, but it previously skipped updating `lastSweepAtMsByStore`. The next cron timer tick therefore treated the store as never swept and re-entered immediately.

This change always arms the per-store cooldown in `finally` after an attempted sweep (success or failure), so the existing 5-minute minimum interval still bounds retries after EACCES / disk-full style failures. No public API or retention policy changes.

## User Impact

Gateway hosts with transient session-store I/O failures no longer enter an unbounded reaper retry loop; failed sweeps back off for the standard cooldown before trying again.

## Evidence

Base: `upstream/main` `4289c6c16cd537288054fee3b1dbd3612c3b9bc6`
Head: `60a1ea6f` (`codex/session-reaper-throttle-on-error`)

Regression test injects `EACCES` from `listSessionEntries` and asserts:

1. first attempt logs `cron-reaper: failed to sweep session store` and returns `{ swept: false, pruned: 0 }`
2. retry 1s later is throttled (no second list call / no second warn)
3. retry after 5 minutes attempts again once

Command:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts
```

Result: `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 20 passed (20)`

Also: `oxfmt --check` on the touched files; `git diff --check` clean.
